C1.why: Medi self-corrected to 'بصوت عالي' before Amal reacted. She just echoed his correct phrase.

C2.why: He struggled to form 'I didn't plan' and produced 'ما خطت', which Amal misunderstood as 'مخطط'. Eventually she helped him arrive at 'ما خططت', correcting his past tense.

C3.why: He used 'هذا يوم الخميس' to mean the coming Thursday, and Amal explicitly corrected him to use 'الخميس الجاي'.

C4.why: Medi self-corrected from 'واحد' to 'واحدة' before Amal reacted.

C5.why: He used masculine 'كان' with the feminine noun 'مرة', and Amal prompted him to change it to 'كانت'.

C6.why: He mumbled a non-word ('tlat'), then switched to English to ask for the word ('I met'). Asking for a word you don't know is not counted as a slip.

C7.why: He missed the fixed preposition 'مع' after 'التقيت', and Amal explicitly prompted him to add it.

C8.why: He incorrectly used 'لأول' on its own to mean 'for the first time', and Amal recast it as 'لأول مرة'.

C10.why: He made the same mistake again, using masculine 'كان' instead of 'كانت', and Amal recast it.

C11.why: He used a number plus plural ('تنتين سنين') instead of the dual form for time units ('سنتين'). Amal explicitly prompted for the correct form.

C12.why: Duplicate of C13, which describes the moment better.

C13.why: He fronted the object but missed the resumptive pronoun '-o' on the verb. Amal named the rule ('You have to point back to it'), leading him to fix it.

C14.why: He made the same fronted-object pronoun omission a second time. Amal prompted him, and he fixed it.

C15.why: He incorrectly used 'في' instead of 'على' for 'at dinner'. Amal explicitly corrected it by saying 'We say on dinner'.

C16.why: He self-corrected 'حلوة' to 'حلو' before Amal reacted.

C17.why: He dropped the 'el-' on the noun in a definite noun-adjective phrase. Amal recast it with the prefix.

C18.why: He incorrectly used 'كليًا' to mean 'in general'. Amal explicitly corrected him to 'بشكل عام'.

C20.why: He missed the 'el-' on 'الأكل', changing the meaning to 'every food' instead of 'all the food'. Amal pointed it out, and he fixed it.

C21.why: He missed the 'el-' on the noun again, and Amal recast it again.

C22.why: He struggled with the word order and gender of the noun-adjective phrase, and Amal fully recast it as 'الأكلة الخضرا'.

C23.why: He placed 'كمان' before the noun to mean 'also', and Amal explicitly taught him that it needs to go at the end of the sentence for this meaning.

C24.why: He stacked possession incorrectly without the proper linking preposition. Amal explicitly recast and later rejected his construction.

C25.why: He used the masculine adjective 'المفضل' for the feminine noun 'أكلة'. Amal recast it to 'المفضلة'.

C27.why: Duplicate of C28, which captures the correction more thoroughly.

C28.why: He incorrectly used the singular adjective 'مفضلة' for the plural noun, and Amal recast it to 'مفضلين' while prompting him for the correct sentence structure.

C30.why: He dropped the 'el-' on the noun before 'تاني', and Amal explicitly quoted his mistake and corrected it to 'الطريق التاني'.

C32.why: He used the adjective 'خايف' (scared) instead of the causative verb form 'بيخوف' (scary). Amal explicitly corrected and prompted him to the right form.

C34.why: He placed 'كمان' after the noun when meaning 'another', and Amal prompted him to put it before the noun.

C35.why: He left the adjective 'تاني' dangling without a noun, and Amal prompted him to add 'واحد'.

C36.why: He dropped the attached pronoun for 'it' after 'عشان', and Amal corrected him by explaining the rule and giving the form 'عشانه'.

C37.why: He omitted the present-tense 'b-' prefix on the verb, and Amal explicitly prompted him to add it.

C39.why: He added the preposition 'لـ' after the verb 'بيبسط' when it takes a direct object, and Amal explicitly corrected him.

C40.why: He missed the 'el-' on the first word of the definite noun-adjective phrase 'الإشي التاني', and Amal recast it.

C41.why: He was explaining a grammar rule in English and got the English meaning slightly wrong. Rule discussions and English phrasing are not Arabic slips.

C42.why: Although in the context of summarizing rules, he actively produced the wrong Arabic phrase 'أغلب إشي' (omitting el-), and Amal explicitly corrected it to 'أغلب الإشي'.

C43.why: During his rule summary, he incorrectly applied 'آخر' as an adjective after the noun, and Amal prompted him for the correct adjective form 'أخير'.
